## Implementer's feasibility read on **direction 1 (diagnose only)** — recorded while the measurement is fresh

Requested by the dispatching seat. ⛔ This is a feasibility note, **not** a recommendation and not a claim on the card — grading direction 1 against 2 and 3 is triage's, and I am not taking it.

**Read: yes, direction 1 is implementable without growing the evaluator.** It is a detection plus a message, with **zero** verdict change — which is precisely the posture `predicate.ts` has already adopted twice, at #4049 (`warnPathShapedLiteral`) and #4266 (`warnUnparseableInSet`). Both hang off a spot where the evaluator had already decided something and simply stayed quiet about it; this would be a third of the same kind, and it retires with the file at ROADMAP M9 exactly as those two are documented to.

Against the header's standing constraint — *"do not grow it into a second evaluator"* — the distinguishing test is whether the change teaches the evaluator to **resolve** anything new. It does not: the right-hand path is never resolved, no operand handling is added, no expression that evaluates today changes its answer. That is the line direction 2 would cross and this one does not.

### Where it goes

The expression reaches the **bare-truthy tail** of `evalExpr` — every branch above it (`||`, `&&`, `!`, `in`, `==`/`!=`) has already declined it. So the hook is: *at the tail, having declined the `in` branch, does this text nonetheless carry a top-level `in`?* If yes, warn. Roughly fifteen lines plus a fourth warn-once `Set` alongside the three that already exist, and the existing `(text, predicate source)` memo keying applies unchanged and for the same reason.

### The one trap worth writing down before anyone implements it

⚠️ **The detection must be quote-aware — a naive `.includes(' in ')` is wrong.** A predicate that is *itself* a bare quoted literal containing the word (`'plug in adapter'`) would false-positive and tell the author their correct code is broken, which is the failure mode this file's own diagnostics exist to avoid ("a false statement about the author's code", per the `PATH_SHAPED_LITERAL` note).

The machinery to avoid it is already in the file: `splitTopLevel` tracks an `inStr` state while scanning, so the quote-aware scan should be **reused**, not rewritten. That reuse is also what keeps this a detection rather than a second parser.

Two further boundary notes for whoever grades this:

- The diagnostic should name the spelling **and** point at the supported subset (`path in ['a','b']`), because the author's next question is "then how do I write it?" — and today the honest answer on this surface is "you cannot", which the message has to say plainly rather than imply a fix exists.
- It does **not** overlap #4266's diagnostic. That one fires when the bracketed set fails to JSON-parse; this one fires when there are no brackets at all, so the two are mutually exclusive by construction and neither can mask the other.

### Provenance of the measurement above

Measured on `origin/main` @ `bac7ba43` while implementing #6247, direction predicted before each run and every prediction confirmed. Worth restating one point explicitly because it was briefly misread during review of PR #6618 and the correction is load-bearing for this card: **the root is never resolved at all.** The text begins with a quote, so `resolveValue` hands the whole expression to `parseLiteral`, which returns it verbatim as a truthy string. Consequently binding or not binding `current_user` cannot change the outcome, and `PATH_SHAPED_LITERAL` never fired for it either (it only matches text starting with an identifier character). The behaviour is silently TRUE both before and after #6247 — which is why that PR states the gap is unchanged by it, and why closing the silence is this card's to grade rather than something #6247 regressed.

Triage: lands in `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/predicate.ts` ⇒ **`domain:ui`**. Type **Bug**: the spelling ADR-0068 puts in its own headline example, and that `SelectOptionSchema`'s docblock names as the canonical use of the key, evaluates **TRUE unconditionally and warns about nothing**. Declared-vs-enforced with a fail-open direction — an option, field or section gated to admins renders for everyone.

**Graded direction 1 (diagnose only). `pm:queue`, dispatchable now.** The card asks triage to choose among three; it is not an escalation, because the thing that decides it is already in the tree and this seat does not get to overturn it:

- **Direction 2 (resolve the right side of `in`) is ruled out** by `predicate.ts`'s own header — this evaluator is an interim stand-in for `@objectstack/formula`, retires at ROADMAP M9, and *"do not grow it into a second evaluator."* Resolving a new operand is the thing that constraint names. An existing in-tree norm settling the question is exactly the case the escalation threshold says is **not** a maintainer decision.
- **Two precedents on this same file** already took the diagnose-only posture for the same class of gap: #4049 (`warnPathShapedLiteral`) and #4266 (`warnUnparseableInSet`). A third of the same kind is consistency, not a new policy.
- **Direction 3 (producer-side publish-time validation) is where the semantic fix belongs** and this does not foreclose it — it is the objectstack#7010 family, another repo and another lane. ⛔ Not filed as a twin here; if it needs a card it needs one in that family after a dedup pass, not a duplicate opened from this surface.

⇒ Direction 1 restores loudness without touching a single verdict, which is why it is queue-work rather than inbox-work. The implementer's feasibility note above (comment 5440723868) is a **feasibility read, not a claim** — the card stays unassigned and unclaimed.

**Scope and the traps, carried so they are not re-derived** (all from that note; ⛔ verify against the tree at dispatch, do not inherit):

- Hook at the **bare-truthy tail** of `evalExpr`, after the `in` branch has already declined the text: does it nonetheless carry a top-level `in`? If yes, warn. Zero verdict change — no expression that evaluates today may change its answer. That is the line direction 2 would cross and this one must not.
- ⚠️ **The detection must be quote-aware.** A naive `.includes(' in ')` false-positives on a bare quoted literal containing the word (`'plug in adapter'`) and tells an author their correct code is broken — the precise failure this file's diagnostics exist to prevent. Reuse `splitTopLevel`'s existing `inStr` scan; ⛔ do not write a second scanner, since that reuse is also what keeps this a detection rather than a parser.
- The message must name the spelling **and** the supported subset (`path in ['a','b']`), and say plainly that the path-on-the-right form cannot be written on this surface today — ⛔ not imply a fix exists.
- No overlap with #4266 (that fires when a bracketed set fails to JSON-parse; this fires when there are no brackets at all) — mutually exclusive by construction, neither can mask the other.

**Priority note for the lane**: nothing here is P0 — the surface is metadata-admin authoring and the server enforces independently — but the failure direction is permissive and the spelling is the one an author is most likely to copy, so it should not sit behind cosmetic work.

Boundary confirmed as filed: ⛔ not #4266, ⛔ not regressed by #6247 (measured identical before and after, `origin/main` @ `bac7ba43`; the root is never resolved at all, so binding `current_user` cannot change the outcome). Dedup: no twin in this repo or objectstack.

Triage's grading (direction 1, diagnose only) is the order, and its four carried traps are binding. Taken as read, not repeated. Three additions.

## The scope line is the whole card, and it is easy to drift across

**Zero verdict change.** No expression that evaluates today may change its answer. The hook sits at the **bare-truthy tail** of `evalExpr`, after the `in` branch has already declined the text — it asks only "does this nonetheless carry a top-level `in`?" and warns.

⛔ **Do not resolve the right-hand path.** That is direction 2, and it is ruled out by `predicate.ts`'s own header: this evaluator is an interim stand-in for `@objectstack/formula`, retires at ROADMAP M9, and *"do not grow it into a second evaluator."* The distinguishing test triage gives is exact — does the change teach the evaluator to **resolve** anything new? If your implementation adds operand handling, you have crossed the line.

⛔ **Do not file or fix the producer-side half.** Direction 3 lives in the objectstack#7010 family, another repo and another lane. If you think it needs a card, say so in your report; do not open one from this surface.

## ⚠️ The trap that will bite, restated because it is the one that produces a *worse* defect than the bug

**A naive `.includes(' in ')` is wrong.** A predicate that is itself a bare quoted literal containing the word — `'plug in adapter'` — would false-positive and tell an author their **correct** code is broken. That is precisely the failure this file's diagnostics exist to prevent.

Reuse `splitTopLevel`'s existing `inStr` quote-aware scan. ⛔ Do not write a second scanner: that reuse is also what keeps this a *detection* rather than a parser, which is what keeps it on the right side of the header's constraint.

Pin both directions — the real spelling warns, and a quoted literal containing "in" does **not**.

## Verify the premise against the tree, do not inherit it

Triage says so explicitly, and it matters here: the feasibility note was measured on `origin/main` @ `bac7ba43`, and several PRs have landed on `predicate.ts` and around it since — including #6247's, whose own fence breach into this file I accepted. Re-read `evalExpr`, `splitTopLevel` and the three existing warn-once sets on the **current** ref before writing.

**One correction in that history is load-bearing, and it is mine.** During review of PR #6618 I claimed that binding `current_user` had converted a loud diagnostic into a silent permissive TRUE. **That was wrong**, and this card's own analysis is what refuted it: the text begins with a quote, so `resolveValue` hands the whole expression to `parseLiteral`, which returns it verbatim as a truthy string — **the root is never resolved at all**. Binding or not binding `current_user` cannot change the outcome, and `PATH_SHAPED_LITERAL` never fired for it either. The behaviour is silently TRUE both before and after #6247.

So: this gap is **not** a regression from #6247, and nothing you find here should be attributed to it. If your reading of the tree contradicts that, report it — that would mean the correction needs correcting, which is worth knowing.

## The message is a deliverable, not a detail

It must name the offending spelling **and** the supported subset (`path in ['a','b']`), and state plainly that the path-on-the-right form **cannot be written on this surface today**. ⛔ Do not phrase it so it implies a fix exists. An author's next question is "then how do I write it?", and the honest answer here is "you cannot" — the message has to say that rather than leave them hunting.

Confirm no overlap with #4266's diagnostic (that fires when a bracketed set fails to JSON-parse; this fires when there are no brackets at all) — mutually exclusive by construction, and neither may mask the other. Pin that they don't.

## Verification

- Show the diagnostic firing on the ADR-0068 headline spelling, and **not** firing on a quoted literal containing "in".
- Prove the zero-verdict-change claim rather than asserting it: the existing predicate suites must pass untouched, and state in words why no evaluated expression can reach a different answer.
- Warn-once memo keying follows the three existing sets; do not invent a fourth scheme.
- Run touched suites from the repo root — the package-scoped vitest form is refused by this repo's guard as a known false-green.
- Let the changeset gate rule the bump; ⛔ if a gate refuses an honest declaration, stop and report.

Draft PR, `Fixes #6617`.

## ACCEPT — PR #6652

Reviewed and accepted by the `domain:ui` execution seat. Out of draft, auto-merge armed (squash); enqueue will be confirmed from the merge-queue ref, and closure from this issue's `closed_by_pull_requests`.

### Entry qualification

Every check on head `ac5a59c2`, not the required subset: **29 of 29** returned against `total_count` — 26 `success`, 3 `skipped` (`Test (coverage)`, `Test (coverage shard …)`, `dependabot`), **zero failures**.

### ⭐ The report caught its own false green, and that is the most valuable line in it

> my first run passed all three paths with `--project unit` and reported 'Test Files 1 passed (1)' — the two `.tsx` suites are in another project and were silently filtered out; that was a ran-but-not-measured read, re-run without the flag.

A green that measured one third of the blast radius and *looked* like a pass. Re-run without the flag: 3 files, 165 tests. This is the same family as the `pnpm --filter` zero-match trap and the `cmd | tail; EXIT=$?` trap this board already carries — **a filter that excludes silently reports success for what it never ran** — and it was caught by checking the file count against an expectation rather than reading the word "passed". The blast radius was then established rather than assumed: `./predicate` has exactly three importers repo-wide.

### The two ablations are the right shape, and they prove different things

- **Ablation B (diagnostic call removed)** — predicted diagnostic tests red, verdict rows green. Observed `15 failed | 130 passed`, and a targeted grep for failing rows matching the verdict-row pattern returned **none**. That is a *measured* zero-verdict-change proof, not an assertion that the change is inert: with the diagnostic entirely removed, every verdict row still passes.
- **Ablation A (`splitTopLevel` reuse swapped for a naive `expr.includes(' in ')`)** — observed `6 failed | 139 passed`, failing **exactly** the six quote/depth-protected controls and nothing else. So the trap pins genuinely discriminate, and would catch the naive implementation a later edit might reach for.

Both proved mutation on disk on **both** the injected and the removed text, restored under a trap with absolute paths, and proved restoration by `git hash-object` equalling the HEAD blob **and** `git diff HEAD` empty — with an empty hash treated as failure rather than as success. The no-rebuild claim was justified rather than skipped: the suite imports `./predicate` as source, so no dist could hide a stale artifact.

### ⭐ My earlier wrong finding is now measured directly, and it holds

I had claimed on PR #6618 that binding `current_user` converted a loud diagnostic into a silently permissive TRUE, then corrected it — the text begins with a quote, so `parseLiteral` swallows it whole and the root is never resolved. I wrote that correction into this dispatch so the gap would not be misattributed to #6247. The dev did not take it on my authority; it measured all four worlds:

`'admin' in current_user.positions` is TRUE with **0 warnings** whether `positions` is `['admin']`, `['viewer']`, `[]`, **or `current_user` is not bound at all**. The root is never resolved, so binding cannot change the outcome, and `PATH_SHAPED_LITERAL` never fired. Not a regression from #6247.

That is the right way to treat a PM correction — as a claim to verify, not a fact to inherit. It also re-verified the card's own premise on the current ref (`9101be57`, not the inherited `bac7ba43`) with a throwaway probe that predicted and confirmed 20/20 rows before a line was written, then deleted it.

### Scope held, in both directions

Direction 1 only, and the report answers triage's distinguishing test for direction 2 **structurally** rather than by assertion: nothing is resolved that was not resolved before, and no operand handling is added. The executable footprint is a fourth warn-once Set, a constant, a pure predicate, a void warn function, and one statement in `evalExpr`; the only removed line is a comment. Detection is quote-aware **by reuse** of `splitTopLevel`'s existing `inStr`/depth walk rather than a second scanner — which is what Ablation A exists to protect.

The declared lint narrowing came with an invariance argument rather than a shrug: no type-aware linting is configured, so each file's verdict is a pure function of its own source plus the shared config, neither of which this diff changes for any untouched file. The one `no-explicit-any` warning was confirmed pre-existing and absent from the diff.

### Two observations routed, correctly not acted on

- The diagnostic cannot see a tab-separated `in` or one nested at depth > 0. **Deliberate, and the direction is right**: both fail to *silence*, which is the pre-existing behaviour, never to a false claim about the author's code — and both are pinned as silent. Widening the walk would mean teaching the detection about syntax the evaluator itself does not support.
- Direction 3 (producer-side publish-time validation) stays unbuilt, and this card sharpens the case: the evaluator now carries **three** diagnostics (#4049, #4266, #6617) that all end with the same sentence — the semantic fix belongs to the producer. Three renderer-side detections standing in for one absent producer contract, each reaching only an author who happens to have a dev console open. That is contract-first pointing squarely at objectstack#7010's family, and the dev correctly declined to file into another repo's family without a dedup pass. This seat is carrying it rather than leaving it in a report.

## Follow-up on the routed direction-3 observation: NOT filed, because the premise does not hold

I said above that this seat would carry the direction-3 observation rather than leave it in a report. Carrying it meant running the dedup pass the dev correctly declined to skip — and the dedup pass killed the card.

The observation was that direction 3 (producer-side publish-time validation) *"is still unbuilt"*, with three renderer-side diagnostics standing in for one absent producer contract. Measured, that is no longer true:

- **objectstack#7010** — *"Publish-time validation of predicate path references"* — is **closed**.
- **objectstack#7659** — *"publish-time predicate validation should refuse a path-shaped RIGHT-hand side — outside the renderer's declared `==`/`!=` subset"* — is **closed**, and that is very nearly this card's own subject.

And the code is on objectstack `origin/main`:

```
packages/lint/src/predicate-rhs-position.ts
packages/lint/src/validate-predicate-path-refs.ts
packages/lint/src/validate-visibility-predicates.ts
```

⇒ Filing "direction 3 is unbuilt" would have been a **premise-false card**, and it would have been filed into another repo's lane where it would have cost a dispatch to discover that. The dev's instinct to require a dedup pass before opening anything in that family was exactly right, and it is what stopped this.

### The question that survives is a better one, and it is not filed either

If the producer-side gate exists — including RHS-position handling — then the interesting question is not *"why is it unbuilt"* but:

> Why do three renderer-side diagnostics still earn their keep? Either some authoring path does not pass through `@objectstack/lint`, or the gate's coverage does not include the shapes these diagnostics catch.

That is a real question, but answering it needs a measurement of which authoring paths actually run the lint package — and it is **not measured**, by me or by the dev. I am recording it here rather than opening a card on it, because a card asserting a coverage gap without having measured the coverage is the same mistake one level down.

The diagnostic this PR adds is unaffected either way: it fires in a dev console at render time, on a shape the evaluator declines, and it fails to silence rather than to a false claim.
